title: STORIES OF THE CLASSROOM
text:
THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE 99

STORIES OF THE CLASSROOM

Classroom work in Savoy College went forward with earnestness and in a mood of seriousness characteristic of the dignity of professors imbued, no doubt, in the spirit of the times. Among the students there were always the irrepressible spirits who kept the motto "Keep quiet back there, boys" constantly ringing in the Professor's ears. The following stories related about individual students are characteristic of these conditions.

About the year of 1884, in order to meet the needs of the fast-growing institution the College building had been greatly enlarged; and when completed it was quite a new and commodious structure (it was later called the East addition, and when completed it was quite a valuable building of which we were all justly proud). The lower part was used for recitations, with the upper story arranged and fitted to accommodate the Business and Commercial department; and the basement was to be occupied by the intermediate department with Prof. F. Montgomery as its teacher.

The lower story was fitted up with good taste, with the inside wall being shiplapped with white pine lumber. Among the full quota of students in the department were tables arranged in rows with aisles running between each row.

Now as Bill passed in silent meditation upon the soft white pine planks, so he had made in the wall—just large enough to insert a string with a row of nails in it one end of which was hidden on his desk. As just the size of the hole he had made in the wall, about six or eight inches—in such a manner that the string would make a sound the moment anyone would notice more. The College's official advertisement, however, accused him on the ownership of the wall. A long wrangle among the confederates as to the ownership of the string issued, and nobody, being a person of high noble, took his place, and Mark continued the recitation. There was some giggling quietly to his book, continued the recitation. There was some discussion among his classmates about it, and then, at last and determined in his search, after a close scrutiny to find the maker of the prank, called on his coterie on the wall; and with it the solution of the mystery.
